sources.title: Historical biography: birth, McGill degree, teaching, elections and 2015 inauguration
sources.findings: Read the UN Office for Partnerships historical biography: 25 December 1971 birth; McGill BA in 1994; UBC education programme and Vancouver teaching; 2007 party nomination versus 2008 election; 2013 party leadership; 19 October 2015 majority victory and 4 November swearing-in. Its present-tense prime-minister and SDG-co-chair descriptions are dated, not verified current roles. Institutional praise is not an independent impact assessment. The page does not give the UBC graduation year; that is established separately.

sources.title: Alumni profile confirming Trudeau’s 1998 Bachelor of Education
sources.findings: Read UBC’s alumni paragraph explicitly identifying Trudeau’s Bachelor of Education in 1998 and calling him a former national leader. This is separate from the 1994 McGill BA. Do not confuse a teaching qualification with a law degree, PhD or the honorary credentials of other alumni on the page. No original diploma was inspected.

sources.title: Justin Trudeau Fast Facts: birth in Ottawa, parents, degrees and teaching
sources.findings: Read CNN Editorial Research’s personal facts and selected early timeline, syndicated by KEYT: Ottawa birth on 25 December 1971, full name, parents, 1994 and 1998 degrees, teaching before politics and 14 October 2008 election. Although the page path and publication label say December 2024, its body has been updated to describe him as former prime minister; do not assign every sentence to that original publication date. Private family details and unrelated allegations were not copied into the dossier.

sources.title: Parliamentary roles: Papineau terms, prime minister and party leadership dates
sources.findings: Read the Commons roles and election tables. Papineau service runs from 14 October 2008 through 27 April 2025, with re-elections in 2011, 2015, 2019 and 2021. The database records premier tenure 4 November 2015–14 March 2025, and Liberal leadership from 15 April 2013 through 8 March 2025. These are role-record conventions, distinct from election events on 14 April 2013 and 9 March 2025. Parliamentary service does not end on the premier resignation day. No claim that he still holds a seat.

sources.title: Party leaders appendix: Trudeau elected Liberal leader on 14 April 2013
sources.findings: Read the relevant party-leaders appendix footnote confirming Trudeau’s election as leader on 14 April 2013 after interim leader Bob Rae. Distinguish that event from the roles table’s 15 April commencement. The appendix concerns party leadership, not a nationwide election to the premiership. The full history of all parties was not reviewed.

sources.title: 4 November 2015 swearing-in ceremony captions and oaths
sources.findings: Read the Governor General’s captions documenting the 4 November 2015 swearing-in, administration of the oaths, and the 29th Canadian ministry. The prime-minister ordinal is 23rd, not the cabinet ordinal 29th found in scraped labels. Text and metadata were reviewed, not image pixels or the full recording. The 19 October election and 4 November inauguration are separate.

sources.publisher: Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner
sources.title: 14 August 2019 release: Trudeau II finding under section 9
sources.findings: Read the commissioner’s 14 August 2019 release, including the finding under section 9, Trudeau’s stated concern about jobs and economic consequences, the efforts to influence the attorney general, and the explanation that success was not required for a breach. This was the Trudeau II ethics examination, not a criminal conviction of Trudeau and not merely an untested allegation. The commissioner also reported limits on access to Cabinet confidences; no claim of unrestricted access or an independent reinvestigation is made.

sources.title: Trudeau II Report: selected executive-summary and testimony passages
sources.findings: Read selected executive-summary passages and testimony excerpts in the original Trudeau II report PDF. Section 9 concerns improper advancement of private interests through influence; the report found that Trudeau sought to influence Jody Wilson-Raybould over whether the prosecution director should invite SNC-Lavalin to remediation-agreement negotiations. His employment rationale is recorded as his position, not proof that the pressure was lawful. No full reading of all 2268 extracted lines, audit of underlying witness files, or later criminal-procedure conclusion is claimed.

sources.title: CUSMA implementation statement: 2018 signature, 2019 amendment and July 2020 commencement
sources.findings: Read the implementation statement’s introductory paragraphs: 30 November 2018 signature, 10 December 2019 amendment and 1 July 2020 commencement. Cross-checked actual commencement with Global Affairs Canada’s current Joint Review page, rather than treating the earlier planned date alone as proof of implementation. CUSMA, USMCA, ACEUM and T-MEC are national-language names for the same agreement. No claim of unilateral personal authorship, automatic tariff elimination in every case, or completed 2026 review outcome.

sources.title: September 2021 election: another Liberal minority after the early election
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ September 2021 election report on Investing.com, including the early election, minority government since 2019, failure to gain a majority and need to work with other parties. Its contemporaneous leading-seat figures were still preliminary and are not republished as final totals. The Commons table independently confirms the 20 September vote. Retaining government does not mean winning most popular votes, a separate direct premiership ballot, or a single-party majority.

sources.title: 14 March 2025: Trudeau resignation and Carney swearing-in
sources.findings: Read the short Governor General event record for 14 March 2025: Trudeau presented his resignation shortly before Carney’s swearing-in. This actual sequence fixes the resignation day. It is separate from his January announcement, Carney’s March party election and the later end of Trudeau’s parliamentary service. The archive label does not make the described event prospective.

sources.title: 17 October 2018 regulated adult cannabis framework comes into force
sources.findings: Read Health Canada’s 17 October 2018 release and selected rules. It describes a regulated adult market and continued restrictions, including prohibitions on sale to minors and impaired driving; it is not unrestricted legalization. Government predictions about public-health benefits or criminal profits are not asserted as independently achieved outcomes. Old age limits or possession advice are not offered as current legal guidance.

sources.title: Removal of consumer carbon pricing from April 2025, distinct from industrial pricing
sources.findings: Read Finance Canada’s March 2025 backgrounder: federal fuel charge and consumer-price requirements cease from 1 April 2025, while industrial carbon pricing continues as a separate policy area. The change occurred after Trudeau left office; do not attribute the cancellation to his earlier government or claim all carbon pricing was abolished. Political descriptions of effectiveness are not independent measurements of emissions reduction.

sources.title: 22 September 2026 report of completed Ogden Lecture conversation
sources.findings: Read Brown University’s report of the actual 22 September 2026 Ogden Lecture conversation with president Christina Paxson. It identifies Trudeau as former prime minister and describes discussion of Canada–US relations, AI regulation and civic participation, furnishing recent life-status evidence. Unlike the earlier September 9 event advertisement, this reports completed participation. His remarks about trade and US policy are attributed opinions, not independently verified forecasts or official positions of the current Canadian government. No full video or photo pixels inspected.

sources.title: 7 November 2026 report: Oxford distinguished fellowship announced the previous day
sources.findings: Read Sadeen Mohsen’s Canadian Press report on CityNews, posted 7 November 2026. It reports Oxford’s Friday announcement, 6 November, of a Distinguished Fellowship and World Leaders Circle membership and quotes Trudeau’s response. This is a secondary account of the school release; the school’s primary biography could not be opened, and the foundation listing’s indexed snippet was not reproduced in its readable body. No professorship, new degree, settled teaching load, exact contractual term or actual Oxford campus appearance is asserted. The September 11 Toronto photo caption is not the November announcement date.

sources.title: Ministries appendix: 2015 and 2025 transitions and 9 March Carney leadership election
sources.findings: Read the relevant 2015 and 2025 rows and explanatory text of the Commons ministries appendix. It confirms 9 March 2025 Carney party election and 14 March swearing-in upon Trudeau’s resignation. Its table ends Trudeau’s ministry on 13 March, using a succession-boundary convention, while the roles table and Governor General’s account document actual resignation on 14 March. Preserve the latter event date without silently claiming all tables match. Prime ministers and ministries have different ordinals.

sources.title: FCN16: 2018 pricing statute and removal of Part 1 fuel charges in April 2025
sources.findings: Read CRA notice FCN16 background and current-status sections: the Greenhouse Gas Pollution Pricing Act came into force on 21 June 2018, Part 1 covered fuel charges, and Part 2 industrial output-based pricing. The 14 March 2025 announcement preceded rates being set to zero from 1 April; earlier liabilities were not erased. This operational notice is not a full statutory or current individual-tax assessment. Public text distinguishes historical creation, later cessation of fuel charges and continuing industrial system.

portraitReview.license: European Union attribution/reuse permission; verify image-specific terms before release
portraitReview.unresolved: Commons description dates the scene 12 February 2025; EXIF identifies FRANCOIS LENOIR, EU copyright, capture at 13:53 and editing at 14:14 that day. Sikander uploaded the 1561×2342, 2.1 MB version on 13 March, not a new capture date. Commons uses an attribution permission template naming European Commission, whereas the linked original is in Council of the EU Newsroom; it is not established CC BY or public domain. Read Council general copyright rules allowing reuse with source, preserved meaning and clearly indicated changes, subject to specific restrictions. The exact photo page returned no readable lines and the attempted newsroom legal notice was inaccessible, so image-specific exceptions remain to be checked. Portrait-cache directory is absent. One original download on 18 November returned curl exit 22, 403 and reported HTTP 000. No visual identity, original-colour, crop or sharpness check has occurred.
